hits.name: Bitcoin Archive
hits.text:
Bitcoin hash rate jumped 11% in 30 days. 🚀

Miners are showing confidence.

Bullish! https://t.co/Tvew5pfUiC
hits.hook: Bitcoin hash rate jumped 11% in 30 days. 🚀
hits.draft_en:
Hash rate up. "Miners are confident. Bullish."

Or are miners just reacting to price, months late, because new machines take time to plug in?

If hash rate follows price, it's not a buy signal for $BTC. It's a receipt.

Has anyone tested it as an entry rule, with no look-ahead bias?
hits.draft_quote_en:
My read: hash rate mostly follows price, it doesn't lead it. Rigs get ordered when margins are already good.

What's the actual track record of "hash rate up" as a $BTC buy signal?
hits.video_tip: Overlay $BTC price and hash rate on one chart; point at which line turns first. 15-20s.

hits.name: Bitcoin Archive
hits.text:
BE AWARE: Foundation wallet email and domains have been compromised. 🚨

WAIT before taking any action. https://t.co/2Hw3CN9J3X
hits.hook: BE AWARE: Foundation wallet email and domains have been compromised. 🚨
hits.draft_en:
A wallet company's email and domains get compromised.

Your keys don't change. Your device doesn't either. Unless you "update" from a link in that email.

Air-gapped doesn't make you immune. It shrinks what a fake site or fake firmware can touch.

Do you verify firmware signatures, or do you just click update?
hits.draft_quote_en:
This is the attack surface people forget: not the device, the update channel.

Don't click links. Verify signatures. Wait for confirmation through a channel you already trust.
hits.video_tip: 20s clip: verifying a firmware signature offline before updating (no seed on screen).

hits.name: Bitcoin Archive
hits.text:
Bitcoin ETFs bought $442M last week.

Not enough to reverse October outflows.

Month-to-date: $175M net sell. https://t.co/pEKKG8SjOo
hits.hook: Bitcoin ETFs bought $442M last week.
hits.draft_en:
ETF flows are the new daily horoscope for $BTC.

Inflows: bullish. Outflows: bearish. Both explained after price already moved.

Do flows lead price, or follow it? That's testable.

Until someone shows it, I treat flows as a description, not a signal.
hits.draft_quote_en:
Useful data. The question is direction.

Do weekly ETF flows predict the next week of $BTC, or just echo the last one?
hits.video_tip: Scatter plot: weekly flows vs next-week $BTC return. Let the cloud speak.

hits.name: Dan Held
hits.text: My thoughts on why the concerns around Quantum computing and Bitcoin are overblown👇 https://t.co/TVXn0L8nNs
hits.hook: My thoughts on why the concerns around Quantum computing and Bitcoin are overblown👇 https://t.co/TVXn0L8nNs
hits.draft_en:
"Quantum will kill $BTC." "Quantum is overblown."

Both camps skip the useful questions.

Which coins are actually exposed? The ones whose public key is already on-chain, not every wallet.

How many qubits, how much time, how much money?

And why would whoever builds that machine start with $BTC?
hits.draft_quote_en:
Agree the timelines are usually oversold. But "overblown" isn't "zero".

What happens to the coins whose public keys are already exposed on-chain? And who decides?
hits.video_tip: Whiteboard in 30s: exposed pubkey vs hashed address, and what an attacker would need.

Good evening. 

There are three certainties in life:
1) Death
2) Taxes
and 
3) The relentless and endless debasement of fiat currency.

hits.hook: Good evening.
hits.draft_en:
